tips.comment: A large field maiden, but better is expected of Mukhtalif after his 3rd, beaten a length at Nottingham in his first race after being slow away.
Once again, I have opted for one making its debut from the Gosden stable, who are in great form at the moment. So you can be assured this one could win first time out.

Nicely bred and definite signs of ability in their only 2yo run on Aw @ Wolverhampton over extended 1.1 miles. Solid 3yo comeback over 1.3 miles @ Kempton, top class jockey booked who does so well when riding for this stable and top trainer is best here with his 3yo's last 5 seasons @ 29 percent, making current 7.50 very good Ew value against the hot favourite in the race.

Royal Emblem showed promise when finishing a solid fourth by 4 lengths in a maiden over 8f at Chelmsford on debut. Trained by Edward Smyth-Osborne, who has a good record with improving horses, and ridden by Georgia Dobie, he looks ready to build on that effort after a short break. His stamina will be tested stepping up in trip, but he definitely holds place claims if he stays the distance. Stall 15 is wide but not a huge disadvantage here. An each-way contender in a competitive race with a moderate pace.

I was going to have a maximum each way bet on the selection, but it has taken a huge walk in the market and is now a ridiculous price. On the understanding that I clearly love to lose money, I am still going to back it but to a reduced stake. This is a super race, a 300 thousand Sea the Stars yearling. It has improved and has form that is solid, but at about 6 to 1, has it met a setback? Not a clue. Are the others all Frankel? Who knows?

Cinderella Man did seem to be getting the hang of things after losing the plot but rallied. However, he had done too much and ran out of steam last time out. Worth another shot while dropping to C5 today EW.

Come On Eibhlin, despite her 250-1 odds in the Queen Mary at Royal Ascot, ran on well from stall 1 on the far side to be 9th of 23, beaten four and a half lengths. She should win here, moving up in distance to 6f with Jim Crowley on board.
Made racecourse debut at Newbury when close up in midfield over 6f. Never nearer then, but will have learnt plenty and can improve enough to feature.
The favorite for this race is much too short odds-wise, and it could pay to go each way with this newcomer. The stable is in hot form and capable of producing a debutant winner.

Exhibitioning is a 2-year-old filly trained by Warren Greatrex. She has taken a walk in the betting. She is out of a dam, Lochanthem (GB), a two-time winner and a half-sister to 9 individual winners (amassing 29 wins), five of which posted RPR of 92, 96, 97, 98, and 98. Exhibitioning was a 50,000gns breeze-up 2-year-old, so there is every reason to believe she's a decent-looking filly worthy of the investment.
Slowly progressive but put up a career-best last time out and races today only 2lb higher. Crowley back on board is a plus, and a replication of his last run should put him bang there.

I’m backing Bayadere, the lightly raced 4-year-old Awtaad filly trained by Michael Bell, in tomorrow’s Peter Hughes & ECA Memorial Handicap (Class 6, 1m 2f) at Windsor. She makes her comeback following an 8-month break post wind surgery, and showed encouraging signs when finishing fourth of seven over this course and distance at Ripon last month??'beaten about six lengths off a mark of 65 . That run also saw her backed in the betting, suggesting stable confidence.
Earlier in her career, she was a consistent performer??'no wins yet but multiple placed efforts, notably at Chelmsford and Sandown . Now dropped back into Class 6 company and carrying a modest OR, the handicap project looks well timed. With Hector Crouch taking the ride, he should be able to position her prominently from the outset.

Disappointed last time with connections blaming the quick ground. Prior to that, had run well around here over further, when runner-up off the same mark as today. This represents a drop in class and grade.

A course winner over further here and won over this trip under today's jockey at Bath on penultimate start. Could be suited by the drop in trip and ease in grade after racing over a furlong further in a Class 5 at Newbury last time out.

Albus Anne last won in October when Alec was in the saddle off a 55. The two runs after that in October were to third, with the latest being off a 62. Albus Anne has a history of going well after a break, with the latest being the win on the return in September. Albus Anne has been placed four times after a break. EW 5P.

IMPERIAL CULT hasn't been up to much lately but has now dipped to below last winning mark and drops into this weakish looking race with each-way claims with a potential bounceback on the cards sooner or later. Any rain wouldn't be a problem and the front-running style will also help here.

Ghost Story looks well placed to run a big race today at Windsor. He caught the eye last time out, finishing strongly from an unpromising position in a race where the leaders controlled things early. Despite that, he made good late ground - suggesting he's coming to hand and ready to strike. This evening's race features a few inconsistent types and lacks a standout improver, which opens the door for a more experienced handicapped runner like him. He's back over a mile, which suits him ideally, and the likely stronger pace here plays into his late running strengths.

Not a massive price at 20-1 and could well need this run, which may also be a bit on the short side, but did win a claimer over 1m when in Ireland. Makes stable debut today over this 10f trip. Still has going as good, which with forecast light showers and being an evening meeting, could well change to soft come race time, which will suit. Won last race in Ireland (jumps) and looked to be turning things around, so I give it an each-way chance today.

This selection's best effort to date was a 2nd place finish over the distance of 12 furlongs. Racing back over 10 furlongs in today's contest, hopeful the ground will suit. Taylor Fisher (3) is in the saddle and has each-way appeal.
Won last two in good style, dropping in then coming with a run inside the final furlong. Has a lot of weight but seems to be improving.
NB bet of the day here at a good-looking price. Should run a race of promise and has a good chance of a win. Also, so win bet on cards here.

Some decent form from the 4yo last year. A nice run two weeks ago when beaten around a length, decent rating and the same mark for this handicap. He was coming off a 7 month break that day and he can take a step forward.

This is a fairly hot race, but BISHOP'S CROWN is not without a chance here. Runs well fresh, and the last three outings on the all-weather, which aren't preferred, have served to drop this one down to a tempting handicap mark. Below the weight when last winning on turf, and there are some encouraging runs here in the back catalogue as well.

Harry Did is a consistent performer with two wins and three places from nine runs at this distance and a good record on similar going with a win from three attempts. Wearing a tongue strap that has brought him success before, he finished a respectable fourth last time at Yarmouth despite being a bit below form. Trained by Harry Eustace, who is in good form, and ridden by Pierre-Louis Jamin, Harry Did should be ready to bounce back after a break here. Stall 3 is workable, and he has a solid chance if the pace is strong enough.

Had been in really good form since being switched to the AW and hadn’t been out of the frame in his first four starts on that surface before a disappointing effort at Kempton last time. That was the first start for a couple of months and was too keen. Hopefully, that won't be the case this time, and if that's the case, can reward each-way support.

The Organiser could be worth an each-way bet as he won on the all-weather in March off a 70 at 7f. While the return last month in a Class 4 at 5f didn't work, I think he is worth another shot at 6f today.

A reduced mark and a much-improved run from the 4-year-old three weeks ago. Not the smoothest passage, but he was still a very close 2nd of 14. The 1st and 3rd were both capable runners. Something to build on, and his mark was 16lb higher when he made his debut for this yard in January.

Rival has been consistent at this course and distance with three places from six runs and shows good form on similar going, winning twice from 27 starts. Though still searching for a win in this class, he finished a close second last time, beaten just 2 lengths, and is now receiving a weight pull from that same rival. Trainer James Flint with Saffie Osborne aboard have a good combo rate between them, and stall 3 offers a solid draw. With the mark reduced, Rival has every chance, especially if the pace is honest.
4 places on offer. Unexposed Francisco beat 61% of rivals in 5 runs. Should be good enough to take a place with improvement.
Winner at Yarmouth in April. Struggled off higher marks since but is coming back down the weights and drops back into class 6 this evening so would be no surprise to see him run well.

ADACE is given a look due to the solid-looking course form here last season. Figures read 3225, and all came from around this mark. Has been sailing in all-weather circles since then but makes the return to this sphere with an each-way shout for sure. Wouldn't want too much rain, but will probably be withdrawn if there is.

Going through a barren run as it's now been 12 runs since the last win, which was last year. However, he is moving back in the right direction and was showing good form off a higher mark. So now, running off a mark of 59 presents an opportunity to be competitive.
I got the impression that Raqraaq wasn't really pushed on his last two outings. Although yet to score on turf, he has run two good seconds here off higher marks.

Princess Billyboy spoilt her chances at the start in a Class 2 novice at Newmarket ten days ago as she was slow away and ducked left and then weakened after making up ground. Much better is expected second time out in a weaker race.

Passing Thought is a well-bred filly by Showcasing out of a smart 9f winner, making her debut for Ed Walker, who does very well with newcomers. She is in stall number 8, which is not ideal but manageable over this trip. Kieran Shoemark is a strong booking and should be hopeful of a good run here. Her pedigree hints at speed and some stamina, and the market tells the tale so far. Interesting breed and is a win or each-way chance if supported.

Wren Runner was midfield on debut in a C4 in June. Last time out, she was at the back of the pack in a C3. So I thought we were waiting for handicaps until today's booking of Oisin Murphy and dropping to C5, which makes me think more is expected today.
Arvana Belle looks an intriguing prospect. The 2yo is a half sister to three winners and encouraging signs out of Rod Millman's yard ahead of this one. 20/1 decent value with no standouts.

Trainer Paul Attwater is having probably his best year and that run includes a 2 year old victory. It makes the 33/1 on offer for Denbys Dream a nice price in a race that has seen some longer priced winners in recent years.
Won over this distance at Salisbury last time out to get off the mark at the second attempt. Strong jockey booking for her handicap debut.

Azaniya made all impressively over a mile at Newmarket last month. She goes up in distance to ten furlongs here, but she went away at the finish at Newmarket, and her initial handicap mark looks lenient.
Goes up in distance this evening, and judging from the latest outing, I think this could be a good move by the in-form trainer and should make the frame at least.
Has improved in each of 3 races and followed a close 2nd place at Lingfield with a win at Salisbury in June. Likely to improve further and should be there or thereabouts.
Quick turnaround and step up to Listed class did for her last time. These are calmer waters, making handicap debut in a Class 4. Has an each-way chance with her pedigree.

Kathleen Mary goes over a mile today, and that looks ideal based on her recent running style. She's shaped like a horse who wants a strong test at this trip, staying on well late in her last couple of races, especially when you consider she hasn't been ideally positioned or held up. She's shown enough promise in competitive handicaps to suggest a win is within reach, and this race looks slightly weaker than some she's contested recently. From a decent draw and with a jockey who knows how to run a patient mile, this could be the setup where she finally gets her head in front.

Ridden by one of the best, who has good form on this course. Going is to the horse's liking and has gone the distance a couple of times before. 11th place in a Listed Race, and this is a significant step down.
The heavy going is an unknown factor, but Victor Cee showed vastly improved form last time on the all-weather at Newcastle and looks the likely winner.

Bryan Smart has a couple here at Beverley tonight. With heavy ground being the conditions to race over, that can be testing for these youngsters. This could see this filly, who is by Kodi Bear, giving substance of being ready to strike on debut with Shaw Harrison in the saddle.

I like 3 horses here and have backed all 3. None have had a run, and I was disappointed to see Temple of Athena so short. But with wet conditions, I see a surprise, and Tinkler, a 5-furlong horse which is bred with cut, is worth a punt.

A chance is taken on two year old Dream More making his racecourse debut at 5 furlongs on heavy going. This colt is out of a dam who has produced no less than eleven winners, some useful. The sire, a top class sprinter, got off the mark first time in the July of his two year old season. He also landed a Group 1 on soft ground. The stable saddled a winner yesterday and a treble on Friday.

A low-grade handicap with most runners out of form, but Tootsie ran a good race when second at Thirsk last week. She had shown little in 5 previous starts but, dropped 4 lbs, was beaten less than 2 lengths on good to soft ground. She is off the same mark here and can go one better.

Woodrafff posted his best effort for a while when a close fourth in a classified event over 1m at Ayr and now returns to the same trip in another modest contest. He is in stall number 9, which is not ideal, but he stays the mile well and has shown me he handles good to soft going. John Sullivan keeps the ride, and he runs off a mark of 45, which is very workable at this level. Still lightly raced for this grade, and if building on that latest effort, he could be an each-way contende with a decent pace to aim at for the win also.

She's A Goldigger showed better form in her latest race on soft at Ayr over seven furlongs, where she was three and a half lengths 5th of 14 in her first handicap. She has been dropped two pounds to a lowly mark of 47. Drawn on the outside, she may run prominently.

Is a bit hit/miss form wise, but does have snippets of decent form @ this level and nicely treated off dropping mark of 53. Good apprentice up taking off 3lb and in hands of a shrewd trainer, making current 8/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Firmly at the bottom of the handicap mark with a 5lb claimer in this field and currently not in the best of form. However, her sole win was crucially at this course last May, so hoping with the dropped mark, she has a chance.

Milteye was very game when winning at Carlisle last time. A similar track and going again will certainly be in his favour. The second from the Carlisle race wasn't beaten very far at Redcar on Sunday, so the form looks fair. Cam Hardie rides this time, and he is riding at the peak of his powers just now.

Dr Rio is an old hand at this track, having won five times here. There is some concern as to whether or not he will handle the ground today, but it is possible, considering his sire Rio de La Plata excelled on good to soft. Everything about this race will be familiar to him except the going. He ran once on heavy but in a grade higher. I say the good Doctor will cope.

Ribble River arrives in good nick and continues to hold his form well, placing on his last two starts, including a close third over 12f at Pontefract where he may have gone for home a bit soon. He has placed at this trip and remains on a competitive mark of 67, which looks fair to me. He is in stall number 7, which is workable and handles good to soft ground. Trained by Kevin Ryan and ridden by Tom Eaves, both in decent form. With a more patient ride, he should be thereabouts again. Win player, IMHO, in a race with solid pace.
The going is now officially heavy, which could even up the field. This one has not shown much as of late, but the trainer's in form and could have an outsider's chance in these conditions.
Recobella is unpenalized for winning an apprentice C6 classified race at Nottingham, in which rival Inspiring Speeches was well back in 4th place. Should follow up.
Looks a good bet on this ground, to be fair. Finished 2nd on one try on this ground in a 0-60, down to 0-55 and every chance.

Have You A Minute has not been firing lately but is now well handicapped off a mark of 52 and drops back to 1m, which suits him better. He has placed over course and distance before and is in stall number 1, which is ideal for his prominent handy ride. The going will not be an issue, and with Tom Eaves booked again, there is potential for a sharper run. Trainer T P Tate has got him winning in this class before, and he looks the type to bounce back if things fall right. Win chance if the pace is solid here.

Achieved victory at Redcar in May, but has struggled in three subsequent races. Recently placed 11th in a handicap at Ayr just 15 days ago, showing a lack of effort after encountering difficulties. The 4-year-old's temperament is still a worry, but a modest each-way bet at 25/1 on this distance winner is the most prudent choice.

Has not been able to make strong impressions in all 3 starts to date, but did gain valuable experience here back in May of this year. Is helped by a drop down in class, so has a chance if improvements are made.
WITHOUT FLAW has previously won over the course and distance. The horse did so last time out, winning a Class 6 by 1.5 lengths.

Wichiahpi races off her lowest mark in just over a year ago here, and for me, the jockey switch from the usual jockey is a major positive. The horse is now 4lb lower than her last winning mark and just 1lb higher than her last win on similarly soft ground, which she looks better on. In effect, she has arguably her optimal conditions, a very lenient handicap mark, and a better jockey, so it all points to being decent each way value at 8/1.
One of the few horses that has breeding/results on softer ground. The horse's last run was a solid run. Been tumbling down the weights. I can see this leading from pillar to post.

Blackcurrent had a rare outing on the flat last time and won over course and distance. He could go well again, put up two pounds with Shay Farmer taking off his seven-pound allowance. He is in sparkling form with three of his thirteen wins coming in the last fortnight.

No show Lto, but has been given a nice mini break to freshen them up and this C/D winner is very well handicapped @ this class 6 level off current mark of 58. Good jockey retains ride and very shrewd trainer is best here with his 4yo plus last 5 seasons @ 12 percent, making current 9/1 solid Ew value in the race.

Dandy Fitz encountered soft ground as a juvenile without success, but his two runs last year on good to soft were good runs. He won at Catterick and then followed up at Thirsk, not beaten that far when down the field in a better race. He has been running fairly well this year, and the ease in the going could suit.

I did not have any selections yesterday. This horse will need to seriously improve from the last time out effort when only 11th of 12 at Doncaster earlier this month, but should welcome the dropped mark and is only 2lbs higher than the last winning mark.

May's C&D winner, who also secured another win at Nottingham, ended up 11th in a handicap at Carlisle 26 days ago. This is a more manageable race, presenting a solid opportunity for a winning rebound.
Urban Sprawl ran well on soft at Carlisle in June and also won on soft last October so the heavy going at Beverley might revive his form.

Young Churchill finally broke his maiden tag over hurdles. Although rated considerably lower than Buddy One over hurdles, Buddy One has previously not shown that much talent on the flat. Young Churchill showed a slightly higher rating, and if the going does not go soft, he should be able to hold off Buddy One and the dual bumper-winning gelding Friary Road.

Won two Bumper races over 2 miles at Listowel and Punchestown last September and October. Has run well enough in the last 3 starts this year on the flat all over 1m4f and this extra furlong could well bring enough improvement to see the horse winning today.

This selection's best effort to date was a 3rd place finish over the distance of 24.5 furlongs in a Group 1 over the hurdles. Racing around 13 furlongs and racing on the turf for today's contest, the ground should suit. Rory Cleary is in the saddle. Hopeful it can go close.
Joseph Anthony Murray trains Arch Hall, who may enjoy underfoot conditions with Robert Whearty, who takes off three pounds. He may be having a good night at Ballinrobe. Hope so.

Shane Foley booked for Ken Condon on this 4yo filly by Derby and Arc winner Sea The Stars. Trainer's horses are beginning to run better (one beaten not too far in Group 2 Romanised Minstrel Stakes yesterday). So Golden is unraced but cost 25,000 guineas as a foal. Staying trip could suit, so an interesting entry starting out late at 1m5f.
Buccaneers Spirit is a fairly useful handicapper and looks in a very winnable race if in good form today. Would be giving weight to all of these in a handicap. Good bet.

Captain Hanley is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Ado McGuinness, a trainer in a rich vein of form. He has an unexposed type on his hands in Captain Hanley and should be competitive and have the legs off his much older counterparts. Ado also does very well in claimers, picking up 32 wins in recent years.

Capital Theory lost his way when with Charlie Johnston last season. In his last four races after May, he finished last in three and was well beaten in the other. He has joined the stable of H D McGuigan in Ireland, and his handicap mark did not keep up with his decline in form. So he starts out in a claimer in which he appears to be very well in if retaining some form, and Nicola Burns takes off seven pounds as well.

May Night is now 15 lb below his last winning mark, and while recent form figures do not inspire me, he has slipped to a rating of 51. That gives him a lifeline if the race sets up for a closer. He is in stall number 8, and with 1 win and 3 places on similar going, he is not entirely ruled out if getting cover and settling well. He has won off much higher in the past and could pop up if bouncing back.
Might be the chance for the breakthrough here. Has run in 0-85 handicaps on good to soft and looks sure to be the one here.
Minella Study won a maiden hurdle at Tipperary earlier this month and back on the flat he could be good enough to win this weak maiden over nine and a half furlongs.

This selection's best effort to date was a 2nd place finish over the distance of 12.5 furlongs. It drops to race around 9.5 furlongs in today's contest. Hopeful the ground will suit. Donagh O'Connor is retained. Hopeful it can go close.

Far from embarrassed in two efforts at Ballinrobe and Roscommon so far this term. 5th over this C&D was on similar good ground too and will be all the better for that display. Capable of causing an upset.

Little Boo Thing is a 3-year-old filly trained by J P O'Brien. She hasn't shown much on AW in her first two starts and makes her turf debut today. She is out of a two-time winning dam and is a half-sister to two useful types rated 99-103, Lord Dudley and Dun Na Sead. She is owned by Annus Mirabilis Syndicate, who have had 71 winners with J P O'Brien and A P O'Brien. Today's step up to 9.5f may also bring about some improvement.
Stormie Outlook was a decent 2nd at Roscommon last time and back up two pounds she should go close at Ballinrobe with a decent draw in stall 1.
Three wins from eight starts this season. Career best when winning handicap at Limerick last time out. Thriving, should be bang there.

This selection's best effort to date was a 3rd place finish over the distance of 9 furlongs. Racing around 9.5 furlongs in today's contest, hopeful ground will suit. Robbie Colgan is in the saddle and has each-way appeal.

Deuteronomy can’t keep on winning, can he? If he does, fair play. But at a price, I like the look of BREWEL HILL, who won this race last year. I think he could go well again tonight. He’s back down to 1lb below that winning mark. He needs to step up on his two previous runs, but back down to this mark and Gavin Brouder’s 5lb claim all add to his case. It was yielding to soft last year, and today’s yielding will be welcome, I’d imagine... I do like C/D winners at this venue.

Won 2 claimers for previous stable in May last year. Best run for current yard when runner-up in an apprentice handicap over a mile at Leopardstown in May. Subsequently produced a solid placed effort at Fairyhouse before losing his chance with a slow start last time. Each way value.
This looks like a fantastic each-way chance in this race. Has a great jockey booking on ground and a trip to suit. Could go in under the radar.

In good form on the all-weather earlier this year and returned to turf in April with a very good third at Leopardstown. Hasn't built on that in three subsequent outings but was probably unsuited by fast ground at Leopardstown eleven days ago. Has dropped below last winning mark and should find today's conditions more favorable.
Low weight and has conditions to suit. Ran well when third to Elanor Rosio, keeping on well but just failing. Player.
Derry Lad has not won for over two years but was well-backed last time when running on late into 4th place at Roscommon. Drawn in stall 1 this time, he should be well placed throughout.

San Salvador - a competitive enough handicap, but the yard is flying and the jockey knows how to ride this track. Dual-purpose performer they must think a lot of, because he's been running in much higher grade. Maybe coming back in distance and a bit of ease in the ground will help him carry 10 stone here. Solid bet e/w with four places on offer from most books.

This selection's best effort to date was a 5th place finish over the distance of 12 furlongs. Racing around 13 furlongs in today's contest, hopeful the ground will suit. Chris Hayes is retained and has each-way appeal.
CRISTAL CLERE has posted respectable efforts in defeat this season over distances from around 7.5 to 9.5f. Likely to stay here too and could be one to consider.

La Dame Blanche was a winner over course and distance off current mark of 79 a year ago on soft ground. Second on penultimate start and interestingly tried over 1m5f at Leopardstown three days ago, leading but hanging right at the turn. Slightly less prominent tactics probably will be tried this time. Rory Mulligan claims 7 pounds this time and form-wise has a shout at these weights with suitable conditions. Winner of three of 24 career starts.

Star Harbour rates a strong contender in this handicap at Ballinrobe. He's been holding his form well in far stronger company than this - including a strong effort at the Curragh last time where he finished within a few lengths of some 90+ rated horses. Dropping into this weaker race off a competitive mark, he looks well treated. He's tactically versatile, which is a major plus around Ballinrobe's tight track, and he's proven over the trip. With a capable 7lb claimer taking weight off, and conditions to suit, he brings solid credentials and a class edge to a field where he could shine.

This selection's best effort to date was a 2nd place finish over the distance of 10.5 furlongs. It drops to race around 9.5 furlongs in today's contest. Hopeful the ground will suit. Wayne Lordan is back in the saddle. Hopeful it can go close.
Looks like a good horse with conditions to suit. Stayed on one pace over 7 furlongs, stepping up in trip now and should unlock further improvement.

This is an open-looking handicap, and one that is unexposed at this trip and handicapping is the Kevin Coleman-trained Eutropia. The 3-year-old daughter of Study Of Man was 3rd on her handicap debut despite not getting a clear run, going down by 1 1/4 lengths last time out. By the way, Eutropia was a Roman empress and also means good fortune/well-being. Let's hope that's right this evening.

Galaxy Wonder ran with a bit more promise when third at Limerick last time. Racing freely but sticking on well over a mile, and now steps up in trip which could be the key today. He is in stall number 1, which is ideal if he can settle early, and the addition of a first-time visor might sharpen him up more here. Still unexposed after just four handicap runs and has placed on similar going. Nicola Burns claims 7lb, and the horse has slipped to a workable mark of 53. If settling better, he looks an each-way chance in a race with fair pace and maybe even the win today.
Ran a good race in May in first-time blinkers, but poor last time when blinkers were taken off. Drops in grade today and blinkers are back on. Good draw, trip should be ideal.

Nine furlongs can be within this one's stamina ability. She is by Waldgeist. If anything like her sire, she can be figuring off bottom weight with give in the ground that may be suiting her, answering jockey Killian Leonard's urgings.

Boyne Valley is a 3yo filly owned and trained by Michael Mulvany. Hasn't built on maiden promise, failed to beat a rival last twice. Hard to make a case for other than running off a career low handicap mark of 55 with Wesley Joyce taking off 3lb. She is a full sister to Chain Of Destiny 0-6 but did finish third RPR of 76 in a Leopardstown maiden over a mile. Boyne Valley is stepped up to 9.5f today. She is out of an unraced dam related to six individual winners who were quite decent and performed best mainly over a mile+. Finally, Michael Mulvany has picked up two winners in recent runners: Ina Mina by 15l and Electric Beauty at 14-1 at Leopardstown a couple of days ago, both ridden by Wesley Joyce.

Bhean Saibhre is still a maiden on both the flat and over hurdles, but she finished last season with some promising runs on the flat here and at Navan. Two of them were ridden by Aiden O'Brien's apprentice, Jack Cleary, who rides her again. However, in November, she was put over hurdles and has had eight races showing considerable improvement, finishing 2nd twice. Last time at Roscommon, she made a lot of the running and had regained the lead when unseating two out. A handicap blot down to a mark of 42, as she previously ran respectably off 47 and 49 twice.

Well beaten in first 3 starts all over 1m2f in Maidens, including here. Has since finished a close second over 1m2f here in a Claimer when finishing strongly. So this step up in trip should suit and should go close with an in-form apprentice riding.

Serotonin was unplaced in his first 10 starts but has found improvement in his last two and looks interesting here. He travelled over to Ffos Las off his lowest ever handicap mark and finished 4th, beaten just 3.5 lengths. That was over 2 miles, but he dropped to 1m4f when a fast-finishing runner-up in a Tramore Claimer last week. He steps back up to 1m5f here and looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.
The 11-year-old should run into a place. It has the conditions in which it enjoys and has won very well the last two times on this ground. Chances.

Pretty consistent around here. Beer With The Boys could just wake up here under Nicola Burns, who can also claim 4lb on it after it finally dropped a pound. This is its best track and time of year. EW.

It often pays to side with experience here at Ballinrobe. They don’t all handle this place. You’re always turning and it’s undulating. I’m backing a rag here that has run well here in the past. MAYO FOR SAM finished 2nd here last June for Ado McGuinness, beaten a neck off 57. Won a few runs later in Gowran but has shown little since. He’s back down to a mark of 43 and might be worth chancing at a price but It’s risky.

I am a little surprised that since changing stables, Vicergent has not run in the cheekpieces that saw him come 2nd and then win in them with the prior trainer. But the one thing we know is he likes cut in the ground. I started going through the cards yesterday looking for soft going horses and weather forecasts, but because of possible Rule 4's with non-runners, I thought I'd wait for today and risk losing a decent price. Mark now 58 with a 7lb claimer and runs in this 0-60, and the race he won was a little better than this. But a little more rain will help him today, though the current going is okay.

Artnscrafts is a 6-year-old son of Mastercraftsman ex Lina de Vega, thus a half-brother to Impact Warrior by Saxon Warrior. Last time out, he was 2 lengths second at 20/1 behind Fillyoureye 5/2 by Leading Light in a bumper at Kilbeggan in April. He'll again be ridden by Mr. D Lavery for G Cromwell and in the colors of the Ballylinch Stud. He should improve for his racecourse experience. I make him my Nap of the day.
